title: What If a Lion and a Tiger Had a Cub? It Outgrows Both Parents

scenes.text: What if a lion and a tiger had a cub? It grows bigger than either parent.
A lion father and a tiger mother make a liger. The record holder, Hercules, weighs 922 pounds.
He's almost eleven feet long. Guinness lists him as the largest living cat on Earth.
Swap the parents, tiger father and lion mother, and the cub, called a tigon, is often smaller.
The leading suspect is imprinted genes: growth settings that depend on which parent they came from.
Male ligers are sterile, serious health problems are reported, and fewer than a hundred exist. Every one of them in captivity.

description:
What if a lion and a tiger had a cub? A male lion and a female tiger produce a liger, which typically grows larger than either parent species. Guinness World Records lists Hercules, a liger in South Carolina, as the largest living cat: 418.2 kg (922 lb), 3.33 m long and 1.25 m at the shoulder.
The reverse cross, a tigon, is often smaller. Imprinted genes, whose effect depends on which parent they come from, may explain the difference. Male ligers are sterile, organ, nerve and joint problems are reported, and fewer than 100 are thought to exist, all in captivity.
